limitations: L1 headline: the 'unchanged base' refusal is shadowed by the earlier ancestry control under this round's shape (base is a first-parent ancestor of freeze, observed). P01/P02 (lands=base, freeze=freeze) were refused with 'freeze not on lands first-parent chain', not 'unchanged base'. Derived from observed code order plus observed chain facts: the predicate is reachable only when cfg.base is freeze-or-descendant (degenerate cfg), which no lane probe or selftest fixture exercises. kill_rule's 'refusing the unchanged base is necessary' still holds behaviorally (rc=2 refusal), but the NAMED predicate never fires in the real configuration and the selftest's loose 'refused:' label cannot prove it did.
L2: selftest has no c['legs'] mutation case, so the LEGCOUNT refusal path has zero selftest coverage; alignment is static (frozen LEGS constant vs frozen claims.json) plus observed pass-through.
L3: the runtime grade-order guard ('runtime LEGCOUNT') is likewise unexercised; static reading shows grade() calls match legs order in both claim branches.
L4: 'full commit id required' conflates malformed hex, well-formed non-commit (tree sha) and well-formed absent sha.
L5: refusal text leaks the raw json parse error ('Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)') with no context about which blob failed.
L6: LINT leg is vacuously green when the entry is absent or empty (observed 'CITED-LINES: 0 finding(s) in 1 file(s)' with bytes=0); it gates shape only, never existence.
L7: O's tool authority is the lands blob, unpinned, unlike the freeze-pinned lint sha; the counter measures whatever tool lands.
L8: '# measured revision (lane main)' prints lands verbatim; no control ties lands to the actual lane main HEAD, so any first-parent descendant of freeze measures as 'lane main'.
L9: command() enforces a hard 60s subprocess ceiling; TimeoutExpired escalates the whole claim to refusal rc=2, conflating slowness with refusal semantics.

L10: the except tuple (ValueError,KeyError,OSError,UnicodeError,TimeoutExpired) omits TypeError; a structurally malformed frozen cfg (e.g. non-int min_bytes) would crash with a traceback and an exit code outside {0,1,2}.
L11: no pre-dispatch presence control for cfg-declared freeze blobs such as c['html']; if absent, IRON legs degrade to deterministic mid-run FAIL instead of an early refusal.
L12: ancestry uses --first-parent only; a wave landed via a merge whose second parent descends from freeze would refuse, so landing must stay linear on the freeze chain.
L13: FROZENCFG is vacuously green while lands==freeze (P14); it only bites once lands advances beyond freeze.
L14: selftest fixture cfg is shallow (min_bytes=1, 12 bullets across the 3 ids); it exercises leg plumbing, not the real 6000-byte threshold, which lives in frozen claims.json.
